title: Background of the Study: Examples and Format | AnswerThis
summary: The background of the study explains the context, the problem and the gap behind your thesis. See what to include, six steps and a full example.
body_markdown:
The background of the study is the part of Chapter 1 that explains the context of your research problem. It tells the reader what is happening, what is already known and what is still missing, so your study makes sense.


This guide explains where the section goes and what to include. It then shows how to write it in six steps and gives a full example with a note on each paragraph.


## TL;DR


-


The background of the study moves from the wider context to your own setting.


-


It covers five things: context, problem, earlier studies, gap and purpose.


-


Every fact and statistic needs a source.


-


Length and order differ by school, so check your manual.


## Where does the background of the study go, and how long is it?


In most Philippine theses, the[background](https://www.msuiit.edu.ph/offices/odgp/resources/files/Thesis-Guidelines.pdf) of the study is the first section of Chapter 1. The framework and the statement of the problem usually come after it.


Length differs by school. Your school may ask for less or more, so check your research manual and ask your adviser.


## What should the background of the study include?


A good background covers five things, in this order.


1.


The context. Start with the wider picture, such as the country or the field. Then move to your own province, school or community.


2.


The problem and its size. Say what is going wrong. Use data to show how big it is, and cite the source.


3.


What earlier studies found. Give a short summary of what research already says about the problem.


4.


The gap. Say what is still not known, or what has not yet been studied in your setting.


5.


The purpose. End with what your study will do about the gap.


## How do you write the background of the study in 6 steps?


1.


Collect your sources first. Find recent reports, official statistics and studies on your topic. Note the author and year of each one.


2.


Open with the wider context. Write one paragraph on the topic at the national or international level.


3.


Narrow down to your local setting. Write one paragraph on how the topic looks in your own province, school or community.


4.


Show the problem with data. Give one or two figures that show the size of the problem. Cite each one.


5.


Sum up earlier studies and name the gap. Say what two or three studies found. Then say what they did not cover.


6.


End with the purpose. Write one or two sentences that say what your study aims to do.


## Background of the study example


The example below is for a study titled *Peer Tutoring and the Reading Comprehension of Grade 7 Learners in a Public High School* . The figures mentioned in the first two paragraphs come from the[OECD country note for the Philippines](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/pisa-2022-results-volume-i-and-ii-country-notes_ed6fbcc5-en/philippines_a0882a2d-en.html) . The parts in brackets are for your own data and sources.


### Paragraph 1: the wider context


Reading comprehension is the base for learning in every subject. In the 2022 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), 15-year-old students in the Philippines had a mean reading score of 347. The OECD average was 476.


*What it does: it opens with the wider picture and gives one figure with its source.*


### Paragraph 2: the problem and its size


The same assessment showed that only 24% of students in the Philippines reached Level 2 or higher in reading. The OECD average was 74%. Level 2 is the baseline level of proficiency in PISA.


*What it does: it states the problem and shows how big it is.*


### Paragraph 3: the local setting


The same problem can be seen in \[name of school\]. The reading assessment at the start of the school year showed that \[your school's result, with its source\]. Teachers also observe that \[what teachers report\].


*What it does: it brings the problem to your own setting. Use your school's real data here.*


### Paragraph 4: earlier studies and the gap


Studies have tested peer tutoring as a way to improve reading. \[Name two or three studies you have read and say what each one found.\] However, few of these studies involved Grade 7 learners in public high schools in \[your province\].


*What it does: it sums up what is known, then names the gap. Only claim a gap that your own reading supports.*


### Paragraph 5: the purpose


For this reason, this study aims to determine the effect of peer tutoring on the reading comprehension of Grade 7 learners in \[name of school\].


*What it does: it ends with the purpose, which leads into the statement of the problem.*


## Three short openings from other fields


The first sentences set the direction for the whole section. Here are three openings you can adapt. Add a figure and its source where the brackets are.


### Nursing


Hypertension is a long-term condition, and many older adults need to take medicine for it every day. In rural areas, nurses in health units are often the first people these patients ask for help. \[Add a national or regional figure with its source.\]


### Business


More customers in the Philippines now pay with e-wallets, even for small purchases. Small neighborhood stores must decide whether to accept these payments. \[Add a figure from an official report with its source.\]


### Information technology


Many schools still record attendance on paper. Teachers call names at the start of each class and encode the records later. \[Describe the process in your own school, or cite a study.\]


## How is it different from the introduction, rationale, RRL and significance?


These sections are close to each other, so students often repeat the same points in all of them. Each one has its own job.


Section


What it does


Background of the study


Explains the context, the problem and the gap that lead to your study.


Introduction


In some schools this is another name for the background. In others it is a short opening before it.


Rationale


Explains why the study is needed now.


Review of related literature (RRL)


Discusses earlier studies in detail, usually in Chapter 2.


Significance of the study


Explains who will benefit from the findings.


Our guides on the[significance of the study](https://answerthis.io/blog/significance-of-the-study) and the[review of related literature](https://answerthis.io/blog/rrl-review-of-related-literature) cover those sections in full.


## What are the most common mistakes?


-


Copying the RRL. The background gives a short summary of earlier studies. The detailed discussion belongs in Chapter 2.


-


Statistics with no source. Every figure needs a citation, or the panel cannot trust it.


-


No local context. A background that stays at the national level does not show why your setting needs the study.


-


No gap. If the section does not say what is missing, the reader cannot see why your study is needed.


## Tools that can help you start


The AnswerThis[introduction generator](https://answerthis.io/introduction-generator) drafts three opening paragraphs from the thesis, purpose and context you give it. Write at least 30 words about your study, and you get 3 free runs. It leaves the statistics and citations to you, so add your own cited data to the draft.


The AnswerThis[research gap finder](https://answerthis.io/ai/research-gap-finder) suggests one to three candidate gaps from a search of abstracts, with 3 free runs. Check each gap against your own reading before you claim it.


## FAQs


### How long should the background of the study be?


It depends on your school. Some formats ask for about three to five pages, and others ask for less. Follow your manual.


### Is the background of the study the same as the introduction?


In some schools, yes. In others, the introduction is a short opening and the background follows it. Use the headings in your school's format.


### Do I need citations in the background of the study?


Yes. Cite every statistic, every finding from another study and every policy or law you mention.


### How many sources should I cite?


There is no fixed number. Use enough sources to support the context, the problem and the gap. Recent and official sources are best.
